risks.note: Explicitly listed first among key risks. The Company's stated opportunity set rests on policy support - SATAT, which promotes CBG production and offtake through assured buyback by Oil Marketing Companies, the National Green Hydrogen Mission and innovation schemes such as PRISM - so a change in those frameworks would directly reset the economics of the businesses it is building.
risks.risk: Changes in government policies and regulatory frameworks

risks.note: Named by management as a key risk. The Company has no operating asset in the new verticals - it spent FY 2025-26 assessing potential business avenues and building a foundation, and reports capital commitments of Nil - so the entire biomass-to-energy value chain from captive feedstock to CBG, gasification and hydrogen still has to be executed from a standing start.

Named by management. The innovation vertical depends on moving Passive Radiative Cooling, Phase Change Materials and energy-efficient coatings out of the lab, and the MD&A itself notes that commercialisation rates remain low, with only 10-15% of lab-scale innovations reaching pilot or industrial scale.

Named by management. The intended value chain begins with captive feedstock cultivation, so securing agricultural biomass of the right type, price and reliability is the upstream constraint on any CBG, biofuel or gasification capacity the Company builds.
risks.risk: Availability of suitable feedstock for biomass-based projects

risks.note: Named by management. The Company is loss-making and pre-revenue in its new businesses - the increased loss in FY 2025-26 is attributed to investments in building the new business platform, acquisition-related expenses and corporate restructuring - and it has already turned to shareholders once through a Rights Issue during the year, leaving future scale-up dependent on further capital.

Named by management. India's CBG build-out is being contested widely - 120+ operational plants with 500 under development and 2,212 LOIs issued against the SATAT target of 5,000 plants - so a late entrant with no installed base competes for the same feedstock, sites and offtake.
risks.risk: Competitive pressures and general economic conditions

risks.note: Management explicitly recognises the potential impact of climate-related and environmental risks on its operations and future projects; this matters directly for agriculture-linked feedstock and for the controlled environment agriculture business acquired during the year.

Management states the Company operates in sectors influenced by technological advancements, regulatory developments, market dynamics and macroeconomic conditions, and that it remains exposed to various business and operational risks as it progresses its initiatives in renewable energy, advanced materials and controlled environment agriculture simultaneously - three separate technology and capability bases for a company with effectively no revenue from operations.
risks.risk: Exposure to technological advancement and market dynamics across three unproven, unrelated verticals
